title: Duplicate Order Detector
statement: An online shop receives 1,000,000 orders a day. Support wants to know, for each order, whether the same customer placed an order with the same total in the previous 10 minutes, to catch accidental double payments.
examples: Orders (alice, $30, 9:00) and (alice, $30, 9:04) → second is a duplicate

approaches.name: A hash map from (customer, total) to the last order time, checked in time order
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One lookup per order; old entries can be ignored by comparing times.

approaches.name: A sliding window queue of the last 10 minutes plus a hash set
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also linear and keeps memory bounded, a bit more code.

approaches.name: Sort by customer and total, then compare neighbours
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Works for a daily batch, but not as orders arrive.

title: Team Meeting Finder
statement: A calendar app must find the earliest 30-minute slot when all 12 people on a team are free next week. Each person has up to 200 busy blocks.

approaches.name: Merge everyone's busy blocks after sorting, then scan the gaps
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One sort and one pass over at most 2,400 blocks.

approaches.name: Mark busy minutes in an array for the week
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Simple and fine for one week at minute resolution.

approaches.name: Intersect free times person by person
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct; more steps than merging once.

approaches.name: Try every start minute and check all blocks
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: About 24 million checks; slow and clumsy.

title: Top Songs Today
statement: A music service streams 50 million plays a day across 2 million songs. Every hour it must show the 100 most played songs so far.
examples: Plays a, b, a, c, a, b → top 2: a (3), b (2)

approaches.name: Count plays in a hash map, then keep a min-heap of size 100 over the counts
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One pass to count, and the heap stays tiny.

approaches.name: Count, then sort all songs by count
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct; sorts 2 million songs to keep 100.

approaches.name: Count, then quickselect the 100th largest
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Fast on average; more code and an unordered result.

approaches.name: For each song, count its plays by scanning all plays
approaches.label: unsuitable
